scope: Reviewed rebuild of the clock guest after the 2026-11-16 audit PC-1/PC-2 perp-core changes and the k256 0.14 upgrade (RUSTSEC-2026-0387), and a real Groth16 proof of the reviewed normal fixture under it. Public synthetic test data only; no chain was written to and no proving network or production key was used. The GPU was not in confidential-computing mode and the host is not attested.

superseded.note: an intermediate rebuild and proof of the same day, before the k256 0.14 upgrade; replaced on the branch, never merged

guest_rebuild.first_run: compiled, then refused at the identity check while REVIEWED_GUEST['elf'] still named the earlier guest
guest_rebuild.execution: clock-proof --no-prove once per ELF; the two output directories were byte-identical

host.cuda_runtime_for_server: libcudart.so.12 from the nvidia-cuda-runtime-cu12 12.9.79 wheel preinstalled on the image (prepended to LD_LIBRARY_PATH; the image ships CUDA 13 only)

tools.repository_commit: 8b569ec plus the k256 0.14 change and the REVIEWED_GUEST / sp1-host REVIEWED_ELF re-pin of this commit

prover.groth16_circuit: download_clock_circuit.py pins (archive 18beebb6..., groth16_vk.bin 4388a21c...); the archive was fetched over 16 parallel connections and checked by that script's own verification (archive SHA-256 and size, each file's size and SHA-256)
prover.groth16_backend: gnark on the CPU inside sp1-gpu-server (acceleration=none in its log)
